## Context
The repository from T1 is not useful until the public `BindingStore` facade delegates persistence without changing its mature caller contract.

## Outcome
Route binding load/save and unit-of-work persistence through `BindingRepository` while preserving every public import, constructor, method signature, shared inner dictionary, and caller-visible exception.

## Plan
1. Add facade-focused failing tests for import and signature compatibility, pending/confirmed/reverse lookup, shallow `all_bindings()`, and save/reload bytes.
2. Inject or construct the repository behind the existing facade; keep the facade authoritative and do not expose a writable repository to callers.
3. Preserve existing `peer_state.py` and `get_rotation.py` ownership, rotation-before-live ordering, retired-first move ordering, and best-effort alert semantics.
4. Remove only persistence code made dead by delegation; retain legacy format and exception behavior.

## Testing
Run repository and facade suites together plus the held-out GET-rotation and retired-commit regressions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Existing imports, construction, loader, and public signatures remain unchanged.
- [x] Pending, confirmed, reverse lookup, and shallow `all_bindings()` behavior match the pre-extraction facade.
- [x] Facade save/reload produces the same bytes and exception surface as the direct repository contract.
- [x] Existing peer-state and GET-rotation delegates remain independent owners.
- [x] No caller receives direct writable repository access.

## Out of scope
Lifecycle-policy extraction, rich-emission operations, recovery, and tickets publication changes.
